components.css: .ds-bar { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 4px; padding: 4px; border: 1px solid var(--border); border-radius: var(--radius); background: var(--card); box-shadow: 0 1px 3px 0 rgb(0 0 0 / 0.1), 0 1px 2px -1px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.1); font-size: 0.875rem; } .ds-lang { padding: 4px 12px; border-radius: calc(var(--radius) * 0.8); font-family: 'DotGothic16', monospace; color: var(--muted-foreground); text-decoration: none; transition: background 0.15s, color 0.15s; } .ds-lang:hover { background: var(--muted); color: var(--foreground); } .ds-lang:focus-visible { outline: none; box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px var(--ring); } .ds-lang-current, .ds-lang-current:hover { background: var(--led-panel); color: var(--led); } .ds-bar-sep { width: 1px; height: 20px; margin: 0 4px; background: var(--border); } .ds-ghost { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; width: 32px; height: 32px; border: 0; border-radius: var(--radius); background: transparent; color: var(--muted-foreground); cursor: pointer; } .ds-ghost:hover { background: var(--muted); color: var(--foreground); } .ds-ghost:focus-visible { outline: none; box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px color-mix(in srgb, var(--ring) 50%, transparent); }

narrative.overview:
Japan borrows the grammar of Japanese railway wayfinding (JR and Tokyo Metro signage), seen at night: enamel sign panels, an amber LED departure board, vermilion ink stamps and line colours. Each AllOnFire App is a line with its own colour, and an interface built in Japan reads like a station: you always know which line you are on, where you are, and where the exit is. Density is welcome, decoration is not; a colour appears because it names a line, a state or a piece of station furniture.
 Every page so far is a station moment rather than a tool: the Sign in is the ticket gate (改札), the loading page the platform as a train comes in, the error pages a line that has stopped or a station that is not on it. Each is one centred column on the theme's ground, with one Japanese word brushed huge and faint across the wall behind it. Japanese is signage, never a translation the visitor has to read: the page's own words carry the meaning, and every Japanese mark is hidden from assistive tech.
 It rejects the generic SaaS admin (grey sidebar, white cards, blue buttons that could belong to any product) and anything that slows the task.
keyCharacteristics: One centred column of sign-width content on a quiet ground.
Station furniture (the LED board, the sign band, the field tiles) stays night in both themes.
Vermilion ink for what is pressed on: the hanko seal, the eki stamp.
One brushed kanji, huge and faint, on the wall behind a page.
Day (enamel white) and night (backlit sign black) grounds, following the OS.

rules.name: The Line Rule
rules.body: A line colour means an App. Never use one for decoration or for a state.

rules.name: The Band Rule
rules.body: Colour commits at band or panel scale; a line colour that would appear smaller than a badge is left out.

rules.name: The Furniture Rule
rules.body: A piece of station furniture (a board, a sign's band, a field's icon tile) is night by day too: it scopes `.dark` on itself instead of following the theme.

rules.name: The Signage Rule
rules.body: Japanese is signage: kana and kanji appear on a board, a stamp, a seal or the wall, always `aria-hidden` with `lang="ja"`, and the page says the same in its own language. A board pairs them on one row, the way a real board does; a field never carries a second-language label.

rules.name: The One Voice per Face Rule
rules.body: DotGothic16 is the board's voice and Yuji Syuku the wall's; neither sets a sentence the visitor must read in the page's language.

rules.name: The Hung Sign Rule
rules.body: Only a sign or a floating control casts a shadow; boards, stamps and fields never do.

dos: Do mark an App with its line colour and station badge wherever Apps are listed.
Do keep one Information Blue action per view.
Do give every access state (allowed, denied, pending, revoked) its own shape and label, never colour alone.
Do make browse and edit one keypress apart: records open in place.
Do keep motion short (300 to 700ms), once on entry or on a state change, behind `motion-safe:`; only a board's notice or a loading lamp runs on, and a notice ships its pause.
Do hide every Japanese mark from assistive tech (`aria-hidden`, `lang="ja"`) and say it in the page's own words.
donts: Don't build a generic SaaS admin: grey sidebar, white cards, blue buttons.
Don't add costume Japan: cherry blossoms, torii, rising suns, or a brush face for anything but the one kanji on a wall or in a button.
Don't trade speed for beauty: no motion or ornament that delays a task.
Don't ship pure white or pure black grounds.
Don't shade a board, a stamp or a field: only a sign or a floating control lifts.
